name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan baseline makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely
Donna Miller holds a huge money edge, with $2.7M raised and $4.5M in outside support versus no visible Republican fundraising
Open seat adds some uncertainty, but prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%
Favorable national environment adds several points to Democratic fundamentals
model.rationale: This Chicago-area seat sits D+18, and the Democratic nominee enters the general with dominant fundraising and outside backing while the Republican has shown no measurable financial operation. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late infusion of outside money into the Republican campaign or an unforeseen scandal in the Democratic primary aftermath could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois' second district is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with an 18-point partisan advantage, and Robin Kelly's retirement does not change that underlying arithmetic. Donna Miller, the Democratic nominee, has raised $2.7 million and drawn $4.5 million in supportive outside spending, while her cash position is being replenished by allies. Republican Michael Noack has reported no fundraising or cash on hand.

No public general-election polling exists for the race, and no professional raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and financial disparities. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 96 percent. The seat is expected to remain comfortably in Democratic hands in November.
